messages:
jordan: quick async check-in — doing a late push before PTO, TL;DR: kernel microbatch refactor merged, saw a weird p95 blip on canary, need eyes if you have time
liam: nice, congrats on the merge! what did you change in the microbatcher?
jordan: moved the batch coalescing to earlier in the pipeline and switched to prefetch-first slot allocation; should reduce small-batch overhead
anya: can you drop the PR link? I'll take a look today after standup
jordan: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 — main change is in batcher/coalesce.go, also tweaked KV warmup timing config
liam: seeing the p95 blip on canary logs too — looks like KV cold misses spiking for short sequences
sam: any chance the prefetch window is too small? we've seen thrash if we prefetch across a hotset boundary
nordan: (typo) jordan: fixed — thanks. I increased prefetchWindow from 50ms -> 150ms in the canary, but the Canary runs with smaller slot size which may increase slot steal
liam: can you paste the bench command you used? will run locally
jordan: bench script: 
```sh
./bench --model t0-3b --seq 512 --rps 20 --duration 300 --kv-prime=enabled
```
anya: fyi CI flagged flaky test in kv_cache_test — might be related to timing assumptions
dev-ci-bot: [CI] build/runtime #2489 completed — 1 failed, 12 passed — failed test: kv_cache_test.TestEvictRace (rerun queued)
sam: if kv_cache_test is flaky we should add a short sleep in the test harness rather than masking a race
liam: I can reproduce the p95 locally with jordan's bench after adding a small synthetic coldset; looks like eviction cadence aligns with microbatch drain and triggers extra RPCs
jordan: ok plan: 1) open small follow-up PR to adjust prefetchWindow per slot size, 2) add extra priming in canary config, 3) add TODO in kv_cache_test to stabilize (and a ticket to root-cause race)
anya: sounds good. if you tag me on the follow-up PR I'll review today
jordan: tagged @anya and @liam on PR 4130 (follow-up) — will also post benchmark diffs in the PR description
sam: no blockers from my side; leaving a note for oncall to watch canary p95 for the next 2 deploys :eyes:
liam: LGTM — one nit about log level in coalesce.go but non-blocking
jordan: will fix log level in the follow-up; thanks everyone, grabbing espresso then PTO — ping me if the canary degrades and I'll hop on
dev-ci-bot: [deploy-bot] canary deploy started for runtime:release-2026-03-18-canary
liam: have a good PTO! :coffee: 
anya: enjoy, Jordan :airplane: 
sam: thanks — keeping an eye on metrics, will report back if anything odd shows up
